accuracy.evidence: Checked against the DfE A level Mathematics subject content (statistical hypothesis testing: significance level, critical value, critical region, acceptance region, p-value; actual significance level for discrete distributions), the Pearson Edexcel A level Statistics 1 specification and textbook chapter on hypothesis testing, and the OCR A level H240 specification. Binomial tails were recomputed exactly in the lab's own pmf: for B(20, 0.5) P(X ≥ 13) = 13.16%, P(X ≥ 14) = 5.77%, P(X ≥ 15) = 2.07%, P(X ≥ 16) = 0.59%, so the critical regions at 10%, 5% and 1% are X ≥ 14, 15 and 16 with actual levels 5.77%, 2.07% and 0.59%; for B(20, 0.7) P(X ≥ 15) = 41.6% and P(X ≥ 16) = 23.8%, matching the '≈42% vs ≈24%' power figures. The five judge cases (3.2% at 5% reject, 3.2% at 1% do not, X = 15 reject, X = 14 do not, 6% at 10% reject) and every parameterised answer (n*5 and n for n*100 tests, n for n*20 at 5%) were checked at their corners.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented hypothesis-testing errors in examiner reports (Pearson Edexcel and OCR A level Mathematics principal examiner reports) and the ASA statement on p-values: choosing or changing α after seeing the data (ordering step messages, prediction, mastery m7, challenge tag calc), reading α as the probability H₀ is true (p1, challenge tag ptrue), including a value whose tail is just over α such as X ≥ 14 (lockC miss message, p4, m6, challenge tag over) or stopping short at X ≥ 16 (the 'X ≥ 15 fits too' message, tag under), quoting α instead of the actual level (m3, tags nominal and next), thinking a smaller α is simply better (power step, m2, tags better and easier), and reading 'do not reject' as 'H₀ is true' (step text, m1, tag accept).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagsiglev is built on this topic's own mechanism, the threshold and its consequences: a test-procedure order that refuses data before α, a draggable critical value on B(20, 0.5) that locks only on the largest tail ≤ α for three levels and reports the actual level, a Type I error simulator with H₀ true and a 5% marker, a paired power simulator on a p = 0.7 coin at 5% and 1%, and a reject-or-not judge using both p-values and critical regions. flagtstat (832) builds the null distribution and reads tails; flagnullh (826) writes hypotheses; neither sets α or measures error rates. The gate reports under 30% shingle overlap with every flagship lab, including flagtstat.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each idea arrives through the task: the order step refuses 'Collect the data' before α with the reason; dragging the line shows the tail turn from red to green as it drops under α, and locking X ≥ 16 at 5% is refused because X ≥ 15 also fits; 500 simulated fair-coin tests land at about 2% false rejections, under the 5% marker; at p = 0.7 the 1% bar visibly fills less than the 5% bar; the judge step separates 'below α' from 'not proved true'. Each step's summary appears only after its task.

predictions.evidence: Four predictions with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: when to choose α ('after the p-value' tempts; the order step refuses it), lowering α from 5% to 1% ('bigger region' tempts; X ≥ 15 becomes X ≥ 16), how often a true H₀ is rejected ('never, because H₀ is true' tempts; the simulator rejects about 2%), and the effect of 1% on a real bias ('easier to detect' tempts; the 1% bar catches it about 24% of the time vs 42%). A.reveal echoes the locked-in choice.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions with two wrong options each, every one mapped to its own message: ptrue, data, calc, always, better, easier, rej, accept, over, under, nominal and next, e.g. 'over': 'P(X ≥ 14) = 5.77%, which is over 5%. So 14 is not in the critical region.' and 'nominal': '5% is the chosen level. The actual level is P(X ≥ 15) = 2.07%, because X is discrete.' In-lab misses name the slip too, e.g. '3.2% is under 5% but not under 1%. At this level the evidence is not strong enough.'

readability.evidence: validate_lessons.py passes the learner limits: kid text reads at about FK grade 3 and adult text at about grade 6 (two long adult paragraphs were split on the first pass, from grades 16 and 14). Kid sentences are short ('Say H₀ is true, but you reject it anyway. That is a Type I error.'), and the precise A level terms are used and defined: significance level α, null hypothesis H₀, alternative H₁, critical region, actual significance level, p-value, Type I and Type II error.

no_filler.evidence: No filler pattern matches and explanation overlap with every other lesson, including 832 and 826, is under 12%. Each lab step has one job (order, critical region, Type I rate, power trade-off, decision), and every feedback line carries a probability, a critical value or the rule it breaks. Item explanations give the arithmetic or the reason instead of restating the question.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px in light and dark themes on every step, before and after Show me. First-pass fixes: the order cards 'Find the probability of a result this extreme if H₀ is true' and 'Compare it with α…' overflowed the card at 360 px (shortened to 'Find P(result this extreme) under H₀' and 'Compare with α, conclude in context'), the completed-steps list was 12 px dark green on the dark canvas (now 13 px in the theme text colour with ticks), and the red/green tail readout was low-contrast in dark mode (now lighter red/green in dark). Buttons wrap one or two to a row and stay full-size.

accessibility.evidence: Every canvas action has a button: one per procedure step, '◀ line left', 'line right ▶' and 'Lock X ≥ c', 'Run 50 tests' and 'Run 200 tests', 'Run 100 at 5%' and 'Run 100 at 1%', and 'Reject H₀' / 'Do not reject H₀', each with an aria-label. The canvas aria-label reports the state after every move ('X ≥ 13: P(X ≥ 13) = 13.16%.', '500 tests of a fair coin; H₀ wrongly rejected 8 times, 1.60%.'), and challenge feedback is an aria-live status. walk.cjs reports axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) clean in light and dark on desktop and iPhone 13 with no console errors.
